validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION confirmed independently of GEM. This is the TAPS fuel-gas SUPPLY pipeline (a small-diameter, high-pressure line that carries North Slope/Prudhoe Bay natural gas to fuel the northern TAPS crude-oil pump stations), NOT the large-diameter 1970s-80s proposed Alaska gas export project of a similar name (Alaska Pipeline Project P0146, Denali P0174, ASAP P0293, AKLNG P0147) -- confirmed by two independent documents: (1) Alyeska Pipeline Service Co.'s own 'FACTS' factbook (alyeska-pipe.com, web update dated Jan 2025), which carries a dedicated glossary entry 'FUEL GAS LINE: Carries natural gas received from the North Slope fields from PS 1 to PS 4. It fuels pump stations and cathodic protection systems north of the Brooks Range. In general, it parallels the Dalton Highway, from PS 1 to PS 4,' immediately followed by 'Diameter: 10 inches from PS 01 to MP 34 (34 miles); 8 inches from MP 34 to PS 04 (115 miles) / Length: 149 miles / Pressure: maximum design pressure of 1,440 psi (MAOP)'; and (2) a peer-reviewed engineering paper, Alto & McDevitt, 'Performance of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System Fuel Gas Supply Pipeline' (Arctic Institute of North America / Univ. of Calgary Canadian Permafrost Conference proceedings, pubs.aina.ucalgary.ca), whose entire subject is this specific line: 'a gas pipeline which supplies natural gas to the four northern-most pump stations... extends south from Prudhoe Bay to Pump Station Four a distance of approximately 238 kilometers [=147.9 mi]... grades from 25.4 cm [10 in] to 20.3 cm [8 in]... commissioned in June of 1977.' Both documents are read to exhaustion below (fills[] for every column). PipelineType 'transmission' is also supported: the CPC paper states the line was designed to the requirements of 49 CFR Part 192 ('Transportation of Natural and Other Gas by Pipeline') and ASME B31.8 'Gas Transmission and Distribution Piping Systems' -- a captive, high-pressure utility line built to gas-transmission code, so 'transmission' is the closer of the three controlled-vocab options (never 'gathering' -- it does not collect from wellheads -- and never 'distribution' -- it serves industrial pump stations, not a local low-pressure customer network). No duplicate: checked against the full 42-row roster; the only other Alaska rows sharing 'Trans-Alaska'/TAPS-adjacent naming are the large-diameter proposed export lines listed above, which are a different commodity scope and diameter class entirely, and Point Thomson (P6534, a physically separate FERC-filed transmission line for a different field). CAVEAT: the Owner1 cell warrants a flag -- see the attribution finding below.

validity.researcher_notes: Both independent sources place this pipeline's origin at Pump Station 1, not at Kuparuk. Alyeska's factbook: the FUEL GAS LINE runs 'from PS 1 to PS 4' and elsewhere in the same document, of the TAPS crude system, 'The pipeline begins at Pump Station 1 in Prudhoe Bay.' The CPC paper is explicit and detailed: 'the pipeline design consists of 25.4 cm nominal diameter... pipe from Pump Station One for a distance of 54.7 kilometers [=34.0 mi, matching the factbook's MP 34 transition point exactly] where it transitions to a 20.3 cm nominal diameter pipe for the remainder of its total length of 240 kilometers' and 'extends south from Prudhoe Bay to Pump Station Four.' Neither source mentions Kuparuk anywhere. Kuparuk River oil field (per public reference data, ~70.34N -149.85W) is a physically distinct North Slope unit about 20-25 miles west of Pump Station 1/Prudhoe Bay. The routes-repo geojson for this PID (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7465.geojson, 1 feature, 139 points) starts at (-149.606, 70.324) -- essentially at Kuparuk, not Prudhoe Bay/PS1 -- and ends at (-149.328, 68.417), which IS consistent with Pump Station 4 (documented 'just north of the Brooks Range' by the CPC paper). So: the route's SOUTHERN end (PS4) and the sheet's EndLocation are both right; the route's NORTHERN end and the sheet's StartLocation both appear to share the same Kuparuk-based error, most likely both digitized/entered from the same original mistaken assumption. EndLocation, StartPrefecture/District, Start/EndState/Province and Start/EndCountryOrArea are unaffected (Kuparuk and Pump Station 1 are both North Slope Borough, Alaska, US) -- only StartLocation is corrected in fills[]. Graded RouteAccuracy 'low' rather than 'no route' because the southern ~85% of the traced corridor (from roughly the Brooks Range foothills down to PS4) is plausible and the endpoint (PS4) is right; only the northernmost anchor is off.
